mission: Engineering crawlspace. Desh bangs on a conduit that has been cycling wrong since the extra passengers came aboard. Kael folds himself into the tight space beside him and hands tools without being asked. The smallest warmth between the outsider and the practical man.
why_now: The philosophical scene needed an exit. The ship needs its conduit fixed and the coalition needs a beat that is not an argument. The quietest scene in the chapter does the most lasting work.
conflict: Kael has spent his life being used by institutions. Desh does not use him. Desh asks him for a hydrospanner and Kael has to decide, in the space of one breath, whether being asked is a trap.
turning_point: Kael passes the hydrospanner after a beat of deliberate stillness. Smallest gesture, biggest meaning — first thing anyone has asked him for that was not about the Force.
opening_hook: Desh breaks the silence by banging on a conduit that's been cycling wrong since the extra passengers came aboard.
closing_hook: Kael, watching Desh work: 'You don't feel any of it. The wrongness.' Desh: 'I feel the ship shaking and four Force-users arguing about why.' Kael almost smiles. Almost.
emotional_trajectory: Residual tension -> quiet observation -> the smallest warmth

stakes.personal: Kael's first experience of being treated as a person rather than a category
stakes.interpersonal: Kael/Desh friendship beginning — the outsider and the practical man
stakes.external: Low — this is character breathing room

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — engineering crawlspace, Desh's domain
sensory_details: The ship's mechanical complaints; Desh's competent hands on familiar systems; Kael folded into an uncomfortable space designed for one person; the hydrospanner warm from Kael's grip before he passes it
action_beats: Desh bangs on a malfunctioning conduit and crawls into the engineering crawlspace with his toolkit
Kael folds himself into the crawlspace beside Desh and begins handing tools without being asked
Kael passes the hydrospanner after a beat of deliberate stillness — the first thing anyone has asked him for that wasn't about the Force
notes: Small but load-bearing character scene. Ben is not on stage — the POV stays close to Kael through Ben's absence, observed from the galley or the corridor afterward if needed. Voice: Allston-channel warmth through Desh. Let the hydrospanner do what words would spoil. Anti-pattern: no interiority paragraph explaining Kael's first experience of being asked for help — the gesture is the exposition.
